text.deployment: Inner Sphere forces first encountered the Undine through Clan Diamond Shark trade networks following the Jihad. Four-trooper squads organized in standard Inner Sphere fashion deployed the suit for coastal defense and underwater facility security operations. The Federated Suns proved the most enthusiastic Inner Sphere adopter, studying captured and purchased Undines closely enough to develop their own amphibious battle armor program.

Goliath Scorpion Points of Undine troopers excelled in defensive underwater Trials, leveraging the suit's aquatic mobility and amphibious armament to dominate engagements on their own terms. Five-trooper Points operated primarily from underwater facilities on Scorpion-held worlds, conducting patrols, defending mineral extraction sites, and securing naval installations against rival Clan incursions.

Six-trooper formations of Undine suits saw limited adoption outside standard Clan organization. Those units that fielded the suit in oversized formations did so to maximize underwater patrol coverage, using the additional troopers to establish wider security perimeters around critical submarine infrastructure and deep-sea industrial sites.

The Upgrade variant's land mobility opened the Undine to broader Inner Sphere adoption. Four-trooper squads employed the suit as a light fire support element, pairing it with heavier battle armor in combined-arms formations. The jump-capable Upgrade proved far more attractive to Inner Sphere militaries than the aquatic-only base model, offering genuine tactical flexibility on conventional battlefields.

Goliath Scorpion Points fielded the Upgrade alongside standard Elemental formations for combined ground operations. The Upgrade's matching jump range allowed it to keep pace with Elemental Points while providing LRM fire support, a capability the heavier suit lacked. This complementary pairing of Elementals and Undine Upgrades became a common Scorpion tactical formation for operations where underwater capability was unnecessary.

Six-trooper formations using the Upgrade variant offered conventional land combat capability that the aquatic base model could not provide. These larger formations were occasionally fielded by Clan garrison units that acquired the suits through trade but lacked the underwater infrastructure to exploit the original Undine's strengths, making the land-capable Upgrade their only practical option.

Draconis Combine Admiralty marine squads employ the DCA configuration in four-trooper teams aboard WarShips, DropShips, and orbital installations. These squads specialize in boarding actions and shipboard security, exploiting the variant's close-quarters focus to control corridors and compartments during contested engagements.

Clan Nova Cat naval assets occasionally deploy DCA-pattern Voids in five-trooper Points for shipboard defense and boarding operations. The configuration's emphasis on close combat aligns with Clan boarding doctrine, though Nova Cat warriors more commonly favor their own Gauss-equipped configuration for general surface operations.

ComStar and Word of Blake naval personnel who acquired DCA-pattern Voids organized them into six-trooper Level I marine detachments. The configuration's shipboard optimization made it a useful addition to Com Guard vessel security, though availability remained extremely limited outside Combine space.

Clan Nova Cat forces did not receive the Minelayer variant, as the Combine's Procurement Department chose to withhold production-grade minelayers from the Clan enclaves. This exclusion reflected deteriorating relations between the DCMS and the Nova Cats, and the Minelayer's reduced frame size, which dropped accommodation for Elemental-sized operators, further limited its utility in Clan Points.

Six-trooper Level I formations using the Minelayer configuration could establish significantly wider minefields than smaller squad sizes, leveraging the additional troopers to cover broader frontages. Few units outside the Combine operated the variant, and the Level I organizational option remained largely theoretical given the Minelayer's near-exclusive DCMS availability.

Inner Sphere forces that obtained Nova Cat-pattern Voids through trade or salvage organized them into standard four-trooper squads. The MagShot Gauss rifle's performance made this configuration attractive to DCMS commanders who valued ranged precision, and limited numbers entered service with regular Combine infantry formations.

Clan Nova Cat warriors field this configuration in standard five-trooper Points, where the MagShot Gauss rifle and vibro battle claw combination complements the aggressive close-range tactics favored by Clan infantry doctrine. Second-line garrison clusters received the majority of Nova Cat-pattern Voids across the Irece Prefecture.

The rare ComStar or Word of Blake formations that operated Nova Cat-pattern Voids organized them into six-trooper Level I units. The configuration's Clan-derived Gauss technology made it a high-value salvage target, and captured examples were studied for intelligence purposes as much as fielded in combat.

Draconis Combine Mustered Soldiery units organize their Void troopers into four-trooper squads following standard Inner Sphere infantry doctrine. These squads typically operate alongside BattleMech lances, providing reconnaissance and anti-infantry screening. DCMS elite formations such as the Otomo and the Genyosha brigades received priority allocation during the suit's initial production run.

Clan Nova Cat warriors deploy the Void in standard five-trooper Points, integrating them into Stars alongside OmniMechs. The suit's accommodation for Elemental-sized operators made it one of the few Inner Sphere designs that Nova Cat warriors willingly adopted, with Points serving primarily in garrison and second-line formations across the Irece Prefecture.

ComStar and Word of Blake forces that acquired Void suits organized them into six-trooper Level I formations per their standard military doctrine. These units saw limited deployment given the suit's near-exclusive availability within the Draconis Combine, with most examples reaching Com Guard or Militia hands through battlefield salvage or clandestine procurement.

Inner Sphere commands fielding the Reactive variant organized their troopers into standard four-member squads. The improved survivability of the reactive armor made these smaller squads more durable under fire, partially offsetting the reduced numbers compared to larger Clan Point formations.

ComStar and Word of Blake Level I formations equipped with the Reactive variant gained significant staying power in defensive engagements. Six troopers mounting reactive armor created formidable fixed-position units capable of absorbing sustained punishment while maintaining effective counter-fire against both armored and conventional threats.

Inner Sphere military formations organizing captured or traded Warg suits operated them in four-trooper squads, following standard infantry doctrine. These smaller formations proved adequate for defensive assignments where the Warg's limited mobility was less of a handicap, though fewer suits per squad reduced the concentrated firepower that made the design effective in fixed-position engagements.

Clan Wolf Points of five Warg troopers formed the primary tactical deployment of the suit. Assigned to support frontline OmniMech formations, these Points typically rode into battle aboard Badger or Bandit armored personnel carriers before dismounting to establish defensive positions. The five-trooper Point maximized the suit's combined missile volleys, creating overlapping fields of fire that could stall even heavy BattleMech advances.

ComStar and Word of Blake formations organized Warg suits into six-trooper Level I units when examples became available through salvage or trade. The larger formation size compensated for the suit's slow speed by concentrating more firepower at a single defensive point, aligning with Com Guard doctrine that emphasized holding fixed positions with overwhelming local superiority.

text.overview: The Water Elemental mining suit was a sophisticated submersible exoskeleton developed by Clan Goliath Scorpion for deep-sea industrial operations. Produced at the Hades Industrial Complex on Dagda beginning around 2842, the medium-weight design gave its operators the strength, mobility, and environmental protection needed for underwater mineral extraction and construction work at extreme depths. Though conceived as a purely civilian tool, the Water Elemental proved to be the most consequential industrial development in Clan history, providing the technical and engineering foundation from which all Clan battle armor would eventually descend.
text.capabilities:
Powered by myomer musculature and sealed against extreme underwater pressure, the Water Elemental mining suit achieved its remarkable performance through a network of synchronized micro thrusters linked to thousands of pressure sensors woven into the inner lining. Simple gestures from the operator translated into precise thrust commands, allowing the suit to reach speeds rivaling dedicated submersible transports. The thruster array could also lock the suit motionless against strong currents, enabling precision work in turbulent conditions. Additional buoyancy control devices and depth sensors prevented dangerous rapid ascents while monitoring remaining power and air supply.

As a purely industrial design, the suit carried no weapons. Its equipment loadout included cutting torches, an industrial drill, a basic manipulator for material handling, and a searchlight for low-visibility operations. Two hundred kilograms of standard armor protected the operator from environmental hazards, though this protection was never intended to withstand directed weapons fire. On land, the suit managed only modest walking speed, with its design optimized entirely for underwater mobility.
text.deployment: Five-trooper Points formed the standard configuration for Goliath Scorpion underwater mining operations. Deployed from the Hades Industrial Complex on Dagda, these crews worked mineral extraction sites across Scorpion-held worlds. The Point structure provided sufficient manpower for heavy excavation work and built-in redundancy, ensuring that the loss of a single operator would not halt a critical deep-sea operation.
text.battleHistory:
Clan Goliath Scorpion's extensive underwater holdings demanded specialized equipment for deep-sea mineral extraction and construction. Around 2842, Scorpion scientists at the Hades Industrial Complex on Dagda produced the Water Elemental mining suit, a submersible exoskeleton that gave its operators far greater capability than any conventional diving apparatus. The suit's powered frame allowed workers to perform complex underwater tasks at depths and durations previously impossible. The Scorpions treated these suits as unremarkable industrial tools, deploying them across their underwater mining colonies with little thought to military applications.

That changed around 2860, when visiting Clan Wolf forces on Dagda learned of the Scorpions' mining programs and the exoskeletons powering them. A Wolf Star Captain, recognizing the suits' combat potential, issued a Trial of Possession for one of the units. Point Commander Sarah, assigned the defense, chose her ground carefully. She selected nearby wetlands featuring deep waterways, aggressive fauna, and treacherous footing. Clan Wolf bid a Star of jump infantry against Scorpion operators in their mining suits. Sarah exploited the terrain to devastating effect, using the Water Elementals' aquatic mobility to isolate and eliminate the Wolf warriors piecemeal. The Scorpions lost only a single pilot in the engagement.

Despite the Trial's outcome, Clan Wolf remained determined to acquire the technology. Through merchant caste trade channels, the Wolves obtained Water Elemental suits and began studying their military potential. Engineers added armor plating, jump jets, and weapon mounts to the basic exoskeleton frame. By 2868, these modifications produced a functional combat suit that Clan Wolf first deployed against the Nova Cats. The Elemental battle armor had been born, a design that would reshape Clan warfare for centuries. Clan Hell's Horses subsequently won the technology through Trials of their own, bringing their genetically bred Elemental phenotype warriors into the partnership of suit and soldier that defined Clan powered infantry.

The mining suit's influence extended far beyond the Elemental itself. While Clan Wolf pursued a general-purpose combat design, the specialist prototypes developed during early weaponization experiments inspired an entire family of role-specific suits. The Gnome, Salamander, Sylph, and Undine each traced their conceptual lineage back to those early variants, with the Undine being the most direct descendant of the original underwater design.

Throughout these developments, the Goliath Scorpions continued producing Water Elemental suits at the Hades Industrial Complex for their original mining purpose. Star Commander Vikram demonstrated the unmodified suits' latent combat potential during the Golden Century, pressing a Star of Water Elementals into service on Circe against Clan Mongoose in an unusual underwater engagement. Armed only with industrial tools against scuba infantry, Vikram's forces won a hard-fought battle in flooded terrain, with fierce currents and the exoskeletons' bulk proving as deadly as any weapon. Production at the Hades Industrial Complex continued under Goliath Scorpion control through the Jihad era. Following the Wars of Reaving, Clan Star Adder absorbed Scorpion holdings in the Homeworlds, and the Dagda facilities passed to new management, though the mining suits continued to serve their original industrial purpose.

text.deployment: Four-trooper Anti-Infantry squads serve in Dominion formations organized along Inner Sphere lines, where the smaller squad size allows tighter coordination during building-clearing and urban sweep operations. The reduced headcount concentrates the squad's improved sensor capability into a more manageable element for freeborn infantry officers accustomed to conventional fire-team tactics.
text.battleHistory:
The Wraith traces its lineage to the Rogue Bear, a heavy battle armor prototype first fielded by Clan Ghost Bear garrison forces in the early 3070s. Decades of iterative refinement at BA Facility Gamma on Mannedorf transformed the concept into the production Wraith, which entered Rasalhague Dominion service in 3116. Unlike most Clan battle armor, the Wraith was engineered around interchangeable form factors to accommodate the Dominion's mixed Clan-freeborn military, where standardized Elemental-proportioned suits excluded many otherwise capable warriors from powered armor duty. Quartermasters complained that the variety of frame sizes created a logistical burden, but field commanders valued the expanded recruitment pool.

The Wraith earned its reputation during operations in the late 3130s. In 3137, Rasalhague Dominion forces launched border raids against the Draconis Combine while the Combine struggled with the death of Theodore Kurita. On Schuyler, elements of the Fourth Bear Regulars dropped a Star of battle armor onto the Kurokawa motor pool before dawn and fought building to building for three hours against three companies of conventional infantry. Separately, during Clan-on-Clan skirmishes over worlds vacated by Clan Wolf, two Points of Wraiths championed a flanking assault against the Hell's Horses' 666th Mechanized Assault Cluster on New Oslo, intercepting and eliminating the Cluster's command staff during a withdrawal.

text.deployment: Deployed in standard Clan Points, the Anti-Infantry Wraith fills a specialized role within Rasalhague Dominion combined-arms Stars. Five-trooper Points equipped with this configuration typically anchor defensive positions or lead security sweeps, using their improved sensors to locate concealed infantry while the reactive armor absorbs return fire from fragmentation weapons and light missiles.

Garrison and security commands occasionally organize Anti-Infantry Wraiths into six-trooper formations to maximize coverage during area denial and pacification operations. The larger unit size compensates for the configuration's reduced stealth by providing overlapping sensor coverage and sustained suppressive fire across a wider frontage, an approach favored in rear-echelon and occupation duty assignments.

Inner Sphere military doctrine organizes battle armor into four-trooper squads, and the Rasalhague Dominion adopted this structure for freeborn infantry formations integrated from the former KungsArmé. Wraith squads operating at this strength typically serve alongside conventional infantry platoons, providing heavy fire support and reconnaissance where a full Clan Point would be impractical or unavailable.

Rasalhague Dominion frontline formations deploy the Wraith in standard five-trooper Clan Points, the most common organization for the suit. Wraith Points operate within Stars alongside OmniMechs or other battle armor, leveraging the suit's stealth capability to screen flanks, scout enemy positions, and execute surgical strikes against high-value targets before withdrawing under concealment.

Six-trooper formations reflect organizational doctrines outside standard Clan or Inner Sphere practice. ComStar's Level I structure historically fielded battle armor at this strength, and some Rasalhague Dominion garrison commands adopted the configuration when integrating surplus troopers into existing formations, particularly in rear-area security and planetary defense roles where maximizing each unit's headcount outweighed tactical flexibility.

text.deployment: Marik-Stewart Commonwealth forces organized their Xiphos troopers into standard four-trooper squads, integrating them into combined-arms formations alongside BattleMech lances and conventional infantry platoons. The A configuration’s balanced ballistic loadout made it a favored general-purpose assignment for garrison and defensive units, with squads frequently paired to provide mutual fire support during territorial defense operations.

Following the capture of Washburn’s production facilities, Clan Wolf organized Xiphos suits into standard five-trooper Points. The A configuration’s straightforward ballistic armament appealed to Wolf warriors who valued reliable firepower, and Points equipped with this loadout saw action during the Wolf Empire’s continued expansion, including raids against the Republic Remnant on Alhena where Wolf warriors adopted Commonwealth ambush tactics with mixed results.

Six-trooper formations of the Xiphos occasionally appeared in units with non-standard organizational structures, where commanders grouped additional troopers for increased firepower density. The A configuration’s ammunition-dependent weapons benefited from the larger formation’s ability to sustain fire across extended engagements, though such formations remained uncommon outside of garrison and militia assignments.
